worlds.name: World of Me
worlds.arrival: Kids walk in to mirrors on every table, a body-outline paper roll on the floor, their name on a journal at their spot. Nothing explained.
worlds.room: Mirrors everywhere. Butcher paper for body tracing. Unlabeled baby photos on a mystery board. The Wall blank, the Shelf empty — waiting to be filled by them.
worlds.soundtrack: Quiet. No music Week 1 — the room's own sound (talking, pencils, laughter) IS the soundtrack.
wallQuestions: What's your favorite sound?
What makes you laugh?
What's something only YOU know how to do?
What's heavy?
If you were a color, which one?
worlds.keyMoment: The baby-photo guessing game: a kid sees their baby picture beside their now-picture and feels the 5-year distance that is everything. The room goes quiet for one second. That second is the program landing.
worlds.transition: Cover the mirrors. Leave the feelings maps up. Monday: the room fills with words and 'once upon a time' — the world of stories arrives.

days.title: First Day Ever
days.focus: Arrival. Names. Mood Weather. First verb pick — most kids won't know what to pick and that's perfect. Body trace on butcher paper. Circle head, that's it. Journal given. Cover decorated. Name written (or traced). Declaration: teacher goes first. Books on the empty shelf. Photo of the empty room AND the shelf with just 10 thin journals. This photo matters more than anything else you do today.

days.title: The Mirror
days.focus: Mirror minute: look at yourself for 60 seconds without laughing. Harder than any test. Draw what you see — not what you think you look like, what you ACTUALLY see. Play: fingerprint stamps — press thumb in ink, look under magnifying glass. Name: UNIQUE. Bridge: no two fingerprints in 7 billion humans. Question: 'if everything about you is unique, is it possible to be normal?'

days.title: The Body Map
days.focus: Trace full body on butcher paper (partners trace each other). Label the countries inside: heart = capital city, stomach = kitchen, brain = library, hands = workers, feet = roads. This drawing stays on the wall all 2 weeks. Play: point-to-the-sound game (close eyes, teacher claps from different spots). Name: PERCEPTION. Bridge: same sound, everyone pointed different directions. Question: 'is there such a thing as what really happened?'

days.title: Baby You
days.focus: Baby photo mystery board. Guess who. Laughter guaranteed. Then: what could you do at 1 that you can't now? (cry and get fed). What can you do now that you couldn't at 1? Make the list. The list IS the evolution. Play: the slow stand-up race. Name: GROWTH. Bridge: you grew 3 inches since last year and didn't feel it. Question: 'if you can't feel yourself growing, how do you know it's happening?'

days.title: First Friday
days.focus: Declaration day. Every kid stands: 'My name is ___. My title is ___. And this is my book.' Class responds: 'We see you, [name].' Best writing of the week goes in journal. One Sentence: say your whole week in one sentence. Books on the Shelf. Photo of the Shelf — compare to Day 1. First world reveals. First collection entries. First closing game.

worlds.name: World of Stories
worlds.arrival: Books stand open on every table, propped face-out. A 'story bag' of odd objects sits in the circle. One sentence is written on the board: 'Once upon a time…' with the rest blank.
worlds.room: Cozy. Reading nooks, a story-corner rug, paper for story maps. A shelf of picture books turned cover-out. The Wall has a 'what happens next?' strip.
worlds.soundtrack: Soft instrumental storytime music, low — the sound of a page turning.
wallQuestions: If you could live inside any story, which one would you choose?
Who is the hero of YOUR story?
What's a story only you could tell?
Whose side of the story have you never heard?
How does your story end — or does it?
worlds.keyMoment: The one-word story circle the moment it 'breaks' into laughter and somehow still makes sense — ten kids realize they wrote something together that none of them planned.
worlds.transition: Put the books away. Monday: leaves on the walls, bird sounds, magnifying glasses — the world that was here before any story.

days.title: Once Upon a You
days.focus: Every world starts with 'once upon a time.' Today it starts with yours. Each kid says the first line of their own story out loud — 'Once upon a time there was a kid who…'. Play: the story river — one kid starts a tale, the next adds a sentence, it flows around the circle. Name: NARRATIVE. Bridge: a story is just a chain of 'and then'. Question: 'does your day have a plot?'

days.title: One Word at a Time
days.focus: The one-word story circle: build a whole story with each person adding ONE word. It goes sideways, it gets silly, it somehow holds together. Play it twice. Name: COLLABORATION. Bridge: nobody owns the story; everybody made it. Question: 'who is the author of a story everyone wrote?'

days.title: The Story Bag
days.focus: Pull 3 random objects from a bag. They MUST all be in your story. A spoon, a key, a feather → invent how they connect. Draw the scene. Play: act out your three-object story for a partner with no words. Name: IMAGINATION. Bridge: every invention was once an impossible combination. Question: 'what's a story only you could tell?'

days.title: The Background Character
days.focus: Pick any famous story. Now tell it from the side character — the third pig, the wolf's cousin, the kid in the back. Same events, different eyes. Play: retell a class favorite from the 'wrong' character. Name: PERSPECTIVE. Bridge: the villain is the hero of their own story. Question: 'whose story have you only heard one side of?'

days.title: Story Map
days.focus: Map your story like a place — where it begins, the trouble in the middle, where it lands. Tape the maps up. Best line of the week into the journal. One Sentence: your whole week as a single story sentence. Books on the Shelf. Transition tease: 'Next week the room goes quiet and green — the world that was here long before any story.'

worlds.name: World of Nature
worlds.arrival: The room is different. Leaves taped to the walls, bird sounds playing, magnifying glasses on every table, a potted plant in the center. The mirrors are gone.
worlds.room: Green everywhere. Magnifying glasses at every station. Seed-starter cups (one per kid). A nature table: rocks, sticks, pinecones, feathers, shells. A bug viewer on the shelf.
worlds.soundtrack: Forest ambience — birds, wind through trees, distant water. Underneath conversation, not over it.
wallQuestions: What's the smallest living thing you've ever seen?
What's patient?
If trees could talk, what would they say about us?
What sounds does the earth make?
What's the oldest thing you can see from here?
worlds.keyMoment: The seed sprouting. You can't plan the day — but when a kid comes in and the tiny green thing is THERE, the silence, then the shriek, then everyone crowding one cup on a windowsill: 'IT'S GROWING.'
worlds.transition: Take down the leaves. Leave the seeds on the windowsill — they carry forward. Monday: the room is blue and everything drips and flows.

days.title: The Room Changed
days.focus: Kids notice immediately. 'What happened to the room?' Don't explain. Let them explore for 5 minutes. Touch the leaves. Pick up the magnifying glass. Then circle up: 'Welcome to the World of Nature. For the next 2 weeks, this room is a forest, a garden, and a laboratory.' Plant seeds — one cup per kid. Label with name + date. This cup lives on the windowsill. Check it every single day. Play: the rock-pick game. Name: RELATIONSHIP. Bridge: the rock didn't change, YOU changed by paying attention. Question: 'how many rocks are you walking past every day?'

days.title: Bug Safari
days.focus: Go outside. Find a bug. Don't touch it. Watch it for 2 full minutes. JUST WATCH. Draw what it does. Come back inside. Report: 'My bug was carrying something.' Connect to verbs: bugs CARRY, WAIT, FLOW. Play: the spider-web observation (find one, count connections). Name: ARCHITECTURE. Bridge: the spider was born knowing how to build. What were YOU born knowing? Question: 'what's your web?'

days.title: Sound Map
days.focus: Go outside. Sit still. Eyes closed. 2 minutes. Draw a map of every sound with directional arrows. Come inside. Compare maps — everyone heard different things from the same spot. That's PERCEPTION from Week 1, returning. Play: barefoot walk on different surfaces. Name: TEXTURE. Bridge: your feet have as many nerve endings as your hands. Question: 'what is the ground saying to your feet right now?'

days.title: The Food Chain
days.focus: What did you eat for breakfast? Where did THAT come from? And before that? Draw the chain backwards. Every chain ends at the sun. Everything eats sunlight eventually. Play: domino chain with actual dominoes. Name: CAUSE AND EFFECT. Bridge: one domino of kindness falls into houses you'll never visit. Question: 'if you're mean to someone, how many dominoes fall?'

days.title: Nature Friday
days.focus: Check the seeds. Draw today's cup (probably nothing visible yet — that's the WAIT lesson). Declaration — titles may have nature additions now. '50-step map' activity: map everything within 50 steps of the door. This map will be added to next week. The map is never finished because you keep seeing new things.

worlds.name: World of Water
worlds.arrival: The room is blue. Blue fabric on the walls, cups of water on every table, ocean sounds, a bowl of ice on the nature table.
worlds.room: Blue everywhere. Water stations: cups, funnels, eyedroppers, sponges, food coloring. A clear container in the center. The seeds from Nature still on the windowsill — they need water.
worlds.soundtrack: Ocean waves, rain on a window, a stream — deep and slow. The room should feel submerged.
wallQuestions: Where does water go when it goes down the drain?
What's the oldest water?
If you were a drop of water, where would you travel?
What can water do that you can't?
What does water sound like when it's happy?
worlds.keyMoment: The food-coloring drop in still water — everyone gathered around one clear cup, nobody stirs, the blue blooms outward in silence. 'That's how kindness works. One drop. No pushing.'
worlds.transition: Drain the water stations. Keep the water glasses — they're instruments now. Monday: the room fills with sound and the first language, music.

days.title: The Room Is Underwater
days.focus: Let kids explore the blue room. Touch the water. Play with the ice. Then: 'The water in your cup right now is 4.5 billion years old. It was once in a cloud. Once in a dinosaur. Once in the ocean.' Pour water between cups. Play: pour water into 5 different containers (cup, bowl, plate, bottle, glove). Name: ADAPTATION. Bridge: you're different at school and home, same you, different container. Question: 'are you the same person everywhere?'

days.title: The Water Cycle
days.focus: Map the cycle: ocean -> evaporate -> cloud -> rain -> river -> ocean. It's a circle with no beginning. Like the seed cycle from Week 3. Tape the two circles next to each other. Play: breathe on a cold window — condensation. Name: CONDENSE. Bridge: your breath has water in it. You're raining on the window. Question: 'where does your breath go after you breathe it out?'

days.title: Ice Lab
days.focus: Give each kid an ice cube on a plate. Watch it melt. Time it. What makes it melt faster? Test: hold it, breathe on it, put it in the sun. Play: the salty-water-can't-un-salt game. Name: IRREVERSIBLE. Bridge: words are like salt in water — once said, you can't take them back. Question: 'if you could un-say one thing, what would it be?'

days.title: Sink or Float
days.focus: Bucket of water. 10 objects. Predict: sink or float? Test each one. Chart results. The surprises are the lesson. Play: drop food coloring in still water, watch it spread without stirring. Name: DIFFUSION. Bridge: kindness spreads like the color — drop it in, don't push it. Question: 'what's something you said this week that might still be spreading?'

days.title: Water Friday — HALFWAY
days.focus: Day 25 of 50. HALFWAY. Journey line check — look how far everyone's come. Seed check — growing strong now, needs water. Water xylophone: 5 glasses, different levels, play a tune. Declaration — halfway titles. The Wall gets its deepest water question: 'If water could dream, what would it dream of?'

worlds.name: World of Music
worlds.arrival: Found-sound instruments wait on the tables — cups, rubber-band boxes, rice jars, a row of water glasses. A steady beat is already playing low when kids walk in.
worlds.room: Sound stations everywhere. A 'tuned' water xylophone, body-percussion cue cards, a recording spot for the room's song. The Wall asks 'what does this room sound like?'
worlds.soundtrack: A simple rhythm bed under everything — the kind your foot taps without deciding to.
wallQuestions: If your life had a soundtrack, what would it sound like right now?
What's the most beautiful sound you've ever heard?
Where does a sound go when it stops?
Can you draw a song?
What turns noise into music?
worlds.keyMoment: The room band's first take that actually LOCKS — a beat, a melody, everyone in at once, and the room hears itself become one sound instead of ten.
worlds.transition: Quiet the instruments. Monday: black paper on the windows, glow stars on the ceiling — we leave the ground and go up.

days.title: The First Language
days.focus: Before there were words, there were songs. No talking for the first 5 minutes — only sounds. Hum hello. Tap your name. Play: body percussion — clap, stomp, pat a rhythm, pass it around the circle, keep it alive. Name: RHYTHM. Bridge: your heart has been keeping a beat your whole life. Question: 'what's the rhythm of this room right now?'

days.title: Sound Walk
days.focus: Go outside. Eyes closed. 2 minutes. Collect every sound — near, far, made by people, made by the world. Come back and play your 'sound map' as a song. Play: the hum telephone — hum a tune ear to ear, see how it changes by the end. Name: RESONANCE. Bridge: a sound is just air shivering, and your ear turns the shiver into music. Question: 'where does a sound go when it stops?'

days.title: Make an Instrument
days.focus: Cups, rubber bands, rice in a jar, a row of water glasses tuned by level. Build something that makes a sound on purpose. Tune the water xylophone — 5 glasses, 5 notes, a tiny song. Play: freeze dance — move while the music plays, statue when it stops. Name: PITCH. Bridge: high and low are the same thing moving fast or slow. Question: 'can you draw a sound?'

days.title: The Room's Song
days.focus: Combine yesterday's instruments into one room band. A steady beat, a melody on top, everyone in. Record it — this is the room's song. Play: call and response — the leader makes a phrase, the room echoes it back. Name: HARMONY. Bridge: many different sounds, made on purpose at the same time, become ONE thing. Question: 'what makes noise turn into music?'

days.title: Music Friday
days.focus: Play the room's song one more time, loud. Declaration. Each kid names the soundtrack of their week — 'mine was drums, fast and happy.' Best line into the journal. Transition tease: 'Next week the room goes dark — we leave the ground and go up, way up, into the stars.'

worlds.name: World of Space
worlds.arrival: A dark room. Black paper on the windows, glow stars on the ceiling, flashlights on every table, one lamp glowing in the corner. Kids go 'whoaaa' at the door.
worlds.room: Dark. Glow-in-the-dark stars overhead. Flashlights everywhere. A globe or Earth image. Black paper + white crayons — drawing with light on darkness.
worlds.soundtrack: Ambient space sounds — low drones, distant tones, vastness.
wallQuestions: What would an alien find confusing about our classroom?
What's the farthest thing you can see from here?
If you could name a star, what would you call it?
What's the biggest thing you can imagine?
Does the moon get lonely?
worlds.keyMoment: The Pale Blue Dot: 'that tiny speck is Earth — everyone you've ever met, on that dot.' Then arms wide outside: 'this is how big you think you are; above you, forever.' The room goes still.
worlds.transition: Leave the stars on the ceiling — they stay forever now. Monday: the room softens, pillows appear, and we go inward, to the world you visit every night.

days.title: The Room Is Dark
days.focus: Explore the dark room with flashlights. Cast shadows on the wall. 'Space is mostly dark. The light you see — stars — is rare. But the darkness isn't empty. It's full of things we haven't found yet.' Play: shine flashlight on ball, see day/night. Name: PERSPECTIVE. Bridge: you think it's daytime but someone on the other side is sleeping. Both right. Question: 'can two opposite things both be true?'

days.title: The Pale Blue Dot
days.focus: Show the Pale Blue Dot image. 'That tiny speck is Earth. Everything you've ever known, everyone you've ever met — on that dot.' Stretch arms wide outside: 'Between your fingers is how big you think you are. Above you — forever.' Play: gravity test (drop objects). Name: SCALE. Bridge: your crayon problem feels huge but compared to the universe... Question: 'does being small make you unimportant?'

days.title: Planet Walk
days.focus: Walk the distances between planets scaled to the yard. Earth to Sun = 10 steps. Earth to Neptune = you literally can't walk far enough. 'THAT's how big space is.' Play: the constellation game (connect dots on black paper with white crayon, name the pattern). Name: CONSTELLATION. Bridge: people have been connecting stars into stories for 15,000 years. Question: 'what pattern do YOU see that nobody else sees?'

days.title: Alien Day
days.focus: Invent an alien. Draw it. Name it. Give it 3 habits from the verb cards. 'My alien LISTENS with its feet, BUILDS with its eyes, and SHINEs in the dark.' Write interview questions for your alien. Play: the classroom-from-an-alien's-perspective game. Name: DEFAMILIARIZATION. Bridge: looking at the ordinary as if you've never seen it. Question: 'what would confuse a visitor about the way we live?'

days.title: Space Friday + Message to the Future
days.focus: Write a message to yourself. Seal it in an envelope. Don't open until the last day of summer. 'This is a message traveling through time. The you who reads it will be different from the you who wrote it.' Declaration. Star naming ceremony: each kid names a star after a feeling. Put the names on the ceiling stars. Their constellation is on the ceiling for the rest of summer.

worlds.name: World of Dreams
worlds.arrival: The stars are still up but the room is softer — fabric draped, pillows in the reading corner, sleep masks and dream-journal inserts on the tables.
worlds.room: Soft and dim. The glow stars stay. Pillows, blankets, a 'dream wall' for drawings. Surreal-art supplies — draw the room with everything wrong.
worlds.soundtrack: Soft piano, wind chimes, the sound of slow breathing — vast-internal instead of vast-external.
wallQuestions: Where do you go when you dream?
What's the scariest dream you've had? (it can't hurt you now)
If you could dream on purpose, what would you dream about?
What's the difference between imagining and dreaming?
What's something that only exists when you close your eyes?
worlds.keyMoment: The guided daydream: ten kids, eyes closed under the glow stars — 'in the forest there's a door, you open it…' Thirty seconds of silence while ten imaginations build ten worlds. Then they draw what was behind the door.
worlds.transition: Keep the stars. Put away the sleep masks. Monday: a number line crosses the wall and sand timers sit on every table — the world of time.

days.title: Dreams Begin
days.focus: The room shifts. Stars stay but sleep masks appear. 'Last week we went UP into space. This week we go IN — into the world you visit every night.' Guided daydream: lights off, eyes closed, teacher narrates slowly. 'You're walking on a path...' After: draw what was behind the door. Play: the optical illusion (duck/rabbit). Name: FRAME. Bridge: people are duck-rabbits — your teacher is also a person who watches TV. Question: 'what's the version of someone you've never seen?'

days.title: Dream Journal
days.focus: Every kid gets dream journal inserts. 'Tonight, when you wake up, try to remember your dream. Tomorrow morning, draw it before it fades.' Today: draw a dream you remember. Any dream. Play: surreal drawing — draw the classroom but everything is wrong. Name: SURREAL. Bridge: Salvador Dali painted his dreams. The melting clocks. Question: 'is a dream real while it's happening?'

days.title: Nightmare Flip
days.focus: Some dreams are scary. That's real. Draw something scary from a dream. Then: draw it being silly or friendly. The monster becomes a cartoon. Play: make-a-scary-sound, now make it funny. Name: REFRAME. Bridge: the thing itself didn't change. Your FRAME changed. This works with real fears too. Question: 'what's something scary that's actually funny if you look at it differently?'

days.title: Impossible Inventions
days.focus: Dream logic: anything can connect. Invent something impossible. A chair that flies. A cup that refills. Shoes that sing. Draw it. Name it. Explain what it does. Play: story bag with the weirdest 3 objects possible. Name: CONNECTION. Bridge: every real invention was once impossible. Phones. Planes. Someone dreamed them. Question: 'what impossible thing will be real by the time you grow up?'

days.title: Space + Dreams Closing
days.focus: Gallery: aliens, constellation drawings, pale blue dot responses, dream journals, surreal classrooms, impossible inventions, nightmare flips. Open the time capsules? NO. Not yet. Those wait until Day 50. Transition: 'We went out to space and in to dreams. Next week we go BACK in time. And FORWARD. We enter the world that holds everything: Time.'

worlds.name: World of Time
worlds.arrival: A long paper strip runs the length of one wall. Sand timers sit on every table. Old photos of the neighborhood from decades ago are pinned by the door.
worlds.room: Timers everywhere — sand, digital, a big visible room clock. The wall timeline grows all week. A 'before/after' photo board.
worlds.soundtrack: A slow, steady tick under everything — calm, not anxious.
wallQuestions: If you could visit any time — past or future — when would you go?
Is a minute the same length for everyone?
What's the oldest thing you've ever touched?
What's worth waiting for?
If you can't see time, how do you know it's passing?
worlds.keyMoment: Opening a 'message to the future' from earlier in the summer and reading it aloud — the room feels, for one second, the distance between who wrote it and who's listening.
worlds.transition: Roll up the timeline (keep it). Monday: the room goes warm — cushions, soft light, the mirrors return — the biggest world, the one inside you.

days.title: The Invisible River
days.focus: You can't see it, hold it, or stop it — but it changes everything. The stillness timer: sit perfectly still and FEEL one minute pass. Was it long or short? Play: guess-the-minute — eyes closed, raise your hand when you think 60 seconds is up. Nobody agrees. Name: DURATION. Bridge: the same minute feels long in a line and short in a game. Question: 'is time the same speed for everyone?'

days.title: Before and After
days.focus: Bring a baby photo (or draw 'you at 1'). Three panels: who you were, who you are, who you'll be. Play: the slow-motion race — last one to the wall WITHOUT stopping wins (patience as a skill). Name: CHANGE. Bridge: you grew all year and never felt it happen. Question: 'if you can't feel yourself changing, how do you know you did?'

days.title: The Long Timeline
days.focus: A paper strip across the whole room: your birthday, today, the dinosaurs, the first humans, the first star. See how tiny your strip is next to forever. Play: fast-walk vs slow-walk — who noticed more on the way? Name: SCALE. Bridge: speed makes you miss things; slowness makes you see. Question: 'what are you moving too fast to notice?'

days.title: Message to the Future
days.focus: Write a letter to yourself for the last day of summer. Seal it. Don't open it. 'This is a message traveling through time — the you who reads it will be different.' Play: the four maps of one spot (morning / noon / now / imagined-night). Name: PATIENCE. Bridge: a seed you plant today is a message to a future you. Question: 'what's worth waiting for?'

days.title: Time Friday
days.focus: Look back at the timeline. Declaration — has your title changed since Week 1? Avatar evolution: draw your Week-8 self next to your Week-1 self. Best line into the journal. Transition tease: 'Next week we go inward — to the biggest world of all, the one inside you.'

worlds.name: World of Feelings
worlds.arrival: The room is warm. Fabric draped softly, warm light, the glow stars still overhead, the seeds now full plants. The mirrors from Week 1 return.
worlds.room: Warm tones. Cushions in the circle. Color-mixing cups at the stations. Feeling-body-outline templates. A 'how are you, really?' anonymous wall.
worlds.soundtrack: Gentle — a slow heartbeat sound underneath, soft breathing. The room should feel like being held.
wallQuestions: What does happiness feel like in your body?
What's something that only lasts a moment?
Can you be happy and sad at the same time?
What would you tell a kid who's scared?
What's the strongest feeling you've ever felt?
worlds.keyMoment: The anonymous 'something nobody knows you feel' notes read aloud — the room goes silent, then 'a kid in this room feels these things and we didn't know. Now we do.'
worlds.transition: Leave the feelings maps up. Monday: everything comes off the walls and gets rebuilt as a gallery — the last world, ours, together.

days.title: The Feelings Body
days.focus: Mirrors return. 'We started with YOUR body. We're ending with your body. But now the body map isn't about countries — it's about FEELINGS.' Body outline: color where each feeling lives. Play: color mixing — red + blue = purple. You're never one feeling. You're a blend. Name: BLEND. Bridge: 'how are you feeling' is a trick question because you're always multiple colors. Question: 'is there a feeling nobody's named yet? name it.'

days.title: Mood Weather Deep
days.focus: Check weather 3 times today but this time: DRAW the weather instead of fingers. Morning, midday, afternoon. Three drawings. The weather probably changed. 'Feelings are weather. They move.' Play: the water balloon fragile game. Name: FRAGILE. Bridge: people look solid but one sharp word pops them. Question: 'how full is your balloon right now?'

days.title: Empathy Day
days.focus: Face a partner. Look at them for 30 seconds in silence. Guess how they're feeling. Ask if you're right. Usually you're close. 'How did you know?' 'I could see it in your eyes.' That's EMPATHY. Play: mirror game — copy partner's movements exactly. Name: EMPATHY. Bridge: reading a book and feeling what the character feels. Question: 'when you feel what someone else feels, whose feeling is it?'

days.title: Feelings Evolution
days.focus: Three panels: draw a feeling that started one way and became something else. 'I was scared of the dark. Then I got a nightlight. Now I like the dark.' Fear evolved into comfort. Same three-panel structure as the seed, the dog, the water, the word. Play: Mr. Rogers clip — 'What do you do with the mad that you feel?' Name: RESILIENT. Bridge: bouncing back. Question: 'what's something hard that made you stronger?'

days.title: Feelings Friday
days.focus: The DEEPEST Wall question: 'What's something nobody knows you feel?' Anonymous sticky notes. No names. All displayed. Read them aloud. The room goes silent. 'A kid in this room feels these things and we didn't know. Now we do.' Declaration — this might be the most meaningful Declaration. Some titles will be about feelings now. 'The One Who Feels Everything.'

worlds.name: World of Us
worlds.arrival: The work of nine worlds is coming off the walls and being reorganized into a museum. Journals lie open to Page 1 beside Page 50. The kids become curators.
worlds.room: A gallery. One best piece per world per kid, mounted and labeled. Room-comparison photos (Day 1 empty / today full). The kids' own hummed anthem on a loop.
worlds.soundtrack: The kids' four-note anthem from Music week, played back — their own music, their own room, their own world.
wallQuestions: What will you remember most about this room?
If this room could talk, what would it say?
What's something you can do now that you couldn't on Day 1?
What's your superpower?
What verb will you take home with you?
worlds.keyMoment: The final Declaration on the last day: a kid holds up their fat, messy journal — 'My name is ___. My title is ___. And this WAS my book.' The room answers: 'We see you.' They're glowing. LUMINOUS. They know the word for it.
worlds.transition: There is no next world. The work comes down, the Wall is archived, the journals go home, the stars stay, the seeds stay. Next summer, new kids walk in and see: someone was here before us.

days.title: World of Us Begins
days.focus: Week 10. 'You visited 9 worlds. Now we build the last world — OURS.' The string web game: everyone holds string, passes to someone they learned from, the web connects everyone. Play: the string web. Name: COMMUNITY. Bridge: the web sags without any single person. Question: 'what would this room lose if you weren't in it?'

days.title: Gallery Prep Day 1
days.focus: Choose your best work from each world. One piece per world = 9 pieces per kid. Mount on colored paper. Write gallery labels: title, artist, world, week. The room transforms into a museum. Kids become curators — they decide WHERE their work goes on the wall.

days.title: Gallery Prep Day 2
days.focus: Room comparison photos: Day 1 (empty) next to today. Journals open on tables — Page 1 next to Page 50. Avatar evolution strips complete. Collection grids complete. Practice the Declaration one more time. Practice the gallery walk: 'When someone comes to your work, you say: This is my piece. It's called ___. I made it during the World of ___.'

days.title: Time Capsule + Rehearsal
days.focus: OPEN THE TIME CAPSULES from Day 35. Read the messages from 15 days ago. 'Are you different from the person who wrote this?' Final rehearsal for tomorrow. Final verb pick of the summer. The last reveal is the CUMULATIVE reveal: 'Across 50 days, your most-practiced verb was ___. Your most-visited world was ___. Your title is ___. This is who you became.'

days.title: THE SHOW
days.focus: Families arrive. Kids stand by their work. The room speaks for itself — the Wall, the Shelf, the journals, the photos, the plants, the stars on the ceiling. Each kid does the FINAL Declaration: 'My name is ___. My title is ___. And this was my book.' Past tense. 'Was.' The room responds one last time: 'We see you, [name].' They take home: their journal, their certificate, their printed collection poster, and one verb card — the ONE verb they'll keep practicing forever. They choose. That choice is the last pick. The game continues.
